evidence: Independently re-read specs/behavioral-spec.md (REQ-001..012, full text) and specs/verification-architecture.md (Purity Boundary Map, PROP-001..023, Verification Strategy, Test-Money Safety Rule) this session, plus reviews/spec/iteration-3/output/verdict.json and its FIND-001.json/FIND-002.json (the REQ-003 comparand ambiguity being re-verified), and reviews/spec/iteration-2/output/verdict.json for regression-scope context. ITERATION-3's REQ-003 FINDING (FIND-001/FIND-002, iter3): CONFIRMED-CLOSED. REQ-003's EARS clause (behavioral-spec.md:184-192) now names the comparand `requiredBaseUnits: bigint` consistently with its own Acceptance Criteria (line 205-206: 'baseUsdcBalance < requiredBaseUnits (exact bigint-vs-bigint comparison)') and with verification-architecture.md:13's pure-function signature `checkSourceFunded(baseUsdcBalance: bigint, baseGasBalance: bigint, requiredBaseUnits: bigint, minGasWei: bigint)` -- the 'neededUsd' dollar-float name is gone entirely from both files (confirmed via grep, zero remaining occurrences). REQ-012(c) (behavioral-spec.md:451-455) explicitly ties requiredBaseUnits to the SAME toBaseUnits(capUsd(usdEquivalentOf(need, aktUsdPrice)), USDC_DECIMALS_BASE) bigint value as REQ-002's amount_in and REQ-006's signed tx amount. PROP-005 (verification-architecture.md:66) now carries a nonzero-balance discriminating fixture -- baseUsdcBalance=5000000n ($5.00) vs requiredBaseUnits=toBaseUnits(15.32,6)=15320000n ($15.32) -- which I hand-verified arithmetically: 5,000,000 < 15,320,000 correctly returns false (insufficient), while the described wrong-unit defect (baseUsdcBalance >= neededUsdFloat -> 5000000n >= 15.32 -> true, a real JS bigint-vs-number comparison outcome) would wrongly report funded and fail this exact fixture -- genuinely falsifiable, not merely asserted to be, closing the exact gap PROP-006's zero-balance-only fixture could not catch. REGRESSION CHECK (all remain sound, independently re-verified): REQ-012/REQ-006's base-units cap choke point (behavioral-spec.md:439-492, PROP-019/022 verification-architecture.md:80/83) -- exact-bigint driver-level call-argument assertions for Skip amount_in and BaseSigner tx amount, floor-rounding and wrong-decimals fixtures intact. REQ-005's three-window crash-window nonce requirement (behavioral-spec.md:243-282, PROP-009/020) -- synchronous pre-broadcast 'submitting' record (nonce+leg index) before any broadcast RPC call, call-order assertions intact. REQ-010's destination-address-keyed lock (behavioral-spec.md:387-412, PROP-010) -- still keyed by destination Akash address not route/quote id, dedup-before-price/route-call ordering intact. REQ-009 identity isolation (behavioral-spec.md:366-385, PROP-015/016) intact. Test-Money Safety Rule / PROP-021 (verification-architecture.md:121-136) -- structural static-source-scan over test files intact. NEW GAPS FOUND THIS ITERATION (not present in iter1/2/3 findings, independently discovered): (1) FIND-001 -- `minGasWei: bigint`, the gas-floor comparand `checkSourceFunded` and REQ-003/REQ-004 gate on, is used throughout (behavioral-spec.md:70-76,189-190,199-200,206) but its value/source is defined NOWHERE in either spec file (grep for minGasWei/GasEstimator/estimateGas/gasPrice/MIN_GAS returns zero definitional hits) -- unlike SWAP_MAX_USD, which gets a full explicit single-literal-constant, no-env-override, exact-value treatment (behavioral-spec.md:39-40,307,317-329). REQ-003's own edge case ('a partially-fundable swap that dies mid-signature is worse than not starting') depends entirely on this undefined threshold being real and safe; nothing in the spec stops an implementer from defaulting it to 0n, making the gas check vacuous. (2) FIND-002 -- the same pattern for slippage tolerance: REQ-004 requires 'the acceptable slippage tolerance is an explicit, tested constant' (behavioral-spec.md:236) and REQ-007/verifySettlement's `toleranceBps` parameter (verification-architecture.md:18) is used to gate success/failure, but its numeric value is never stated anywhere, and PROP-013 (the sole proof obligation, verification-architecture.md:74) only exercises the degenerate zero-delta case where any positive tolerance value would pass identically -- no boundary-value fixture exists that could distinguish a correctly-tight tolerance from an arbitrarily loose one. (3) FIND-003 -- REQ-012(c)/REQ-012's Acceptance Criteria (behavioral-spec.md:451-455,489-492) explicitly require the driver's actual `requiredBaseUnits` argument to `checkSourceFunded` be bit-identical, at the call-argument level, to the value simultaneously passed to Skip's amount_in and BaseSigner's tx amount, and explicitly attribute this verification to PROP-005 -- but PROP-005 as literally defined (verification-architecture.md:66) only property-fuzzes checkSourceFunded's pure comparison logic in isolation and contains no cross-call-site driver-level argument-identity assertion, unlike PROP-019's explicit 'inspecting the spies' actual call arguments' treatment of the Skip/BaseSigner pair. This is precisely the class of gap REQ-006 itself warns against ('capUsd() and toBaseUnits() each passing their own isolated unit tests is explicitly NOT sufficient evidence... only the driver-level call-argument assertion is', behavioral-spec.md:313-315) -- but that principle is never extended to the third call site, permitting a driver defect that feeds checkSourceFunded a stale/independently-derived requiredBaseUnits value (distinct from the fresh value used for Skip/BaseSigner) to pass every currently-specified test. Both dimensions FAIL until minGasWei and the slippage-tolerance constant are given explicit, pinned definitions (mirroring SWAP_MAX_USD's treatment) and PROP-005 is extended with a driver-level cross-call-site argument-identity assertion mirroring PROP-019's pattern.
